editorial:
Imagine waking up one morning to find out you just lost your job, only to have a giant pile of cash fall into your lap right after. That is exactly what happens to Gustav and Franz, two best friends working as head waiters in old Vienna. You will love the chemistry between these two; one is a smooth-talking bachelor while the other is a dedicated family man. When they get a sudden windfall of 20,000 dollars from a relative in the US, they decide to buy their old cafe. Instead of keeping it simple, they split the place right down the middle. One side becomes a flashy, modern espresso bar for the youth, and the other stays a classic, quiet coffee house. It is a cozy, lighthearted setup that captures a great era of city life.

What really makes this work is the funny clash between the old school and the new school. You get to see plenty of awkward misunderstandings and silly arguments that test the guys' friendship. While the pacing is a bit slower than today's movies, it feels like a warm hug. If you enjoy classic European comedies, you should definitely track this down. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for a restored version. I suggest adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or check if you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with the family.
endingExplained: After plenty of fighting over their different styles, Gustav and Franz realize that their friendship is more important than their business rivalry. They learn that both the modern music box vibe and the traditional cafe style can exist together. The two friends put aside their egos and combine their efforts to run the cafe as a team. Everything wraps up happily with the business succeeding and the two waiters remaining best friends for life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school comedies and stories about friendship.
